name: miadi-pi-network
description:
Joins a Claude Code session to the Miadi Pi Network as an ordinary peer. The hub (pi/miadi-pi-network) is HTTP + SSE with a bearer token, so this plugin ships the client Claude Code was missing: the `mpn` CLI for register, peers, send, await, inbox, respond, and an unattended `serve` mode that answers inbound prompts with `claude -p`.

<example>
Context: The session needs to know who else is on the network
user: "who is on the pi network right now?"
assistant: "Running mpn peers to list the online peers and their purposes."
<commentary>
Peer discovery is a read against /v1/agents — no registration required to look.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: Another peer holds knowledge this session lacks
user: "ask the pi planner what it thinks of this migration"
assistant: "I'll mpn send to planner with --await and bring back its reply."
<commentary>
The outbound half is a single call; --await blocks until the peer responds or the 30-minute expiry hits.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: The session should be reachable by other peers
user: "make this session answerable on the network"
assistant: "I'll join, then run mpn inbox --wait in the background so an inbound prompt wakes this session."
<commentary>
Claude Code cannot hold an SSE stream between turns; the backgrounded inbox exits on the first prompt, which re-invokes the session.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: A peer must stay reachable with nobody watching
user: "leave a claude peer running overnight"
assistant: "mpn serve --responder 'claude -p' answers every inbound prompt unattended."
<commentary>
Serve is the symmetric-peer mode; its answers pass no human, which belongs in the peer's purpose string.
</commentary>
</example>
